arxiv-2011-15002.title: Image Quality Assessment for Perceptual Image Restoration: A New Dataset, Benchmark and Metric Journal: IJCV Thanks: Dataset and codes are available at https://www.jasongt.com/projectpages/pipal.html .
arxiv-2011-15002.creator: Jinjin Gu 1, Haoming Cai 2, 3], Haoyu Chen 2, Xiaoxing Ye 2, Jimmy S. Ren 4, 5], Chao Dong 3, 6]
arxiv-2011-15002.description: Abstract Image quality assessment (IQA) is the key factor for the fast development of image restoration (IR) algorithms. The most recent perceptual IR algorithms based on generative adversarial networks (GANs) have brought in significant improvement on visual performance, but also pose great challenges for quantitative evaluation. Notably, we observe an increasing inconsistency between perceptual quality and the evaluation results.

arxiv-2108-07190.title: Happy MitM – Fun and Toys in Every Bluetooth Device Conference: 14th ACM Conference on Security and Privacy in Wireless and Mobile Networks; June 28-July 2, 2021; Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates 14th ACM Conference on Security and Privacy in Wireless and Mobile Networks (WiSec ’21), June 28-July 2,
arxiv-2108-07190.creator: Jiska Classen, Matthias Hollick
arxiv-2108-07190.description: Abstract . Bluetooth pairing establishes trust on first use between two devices by creating a shared key. Similar to certificate warnings in TLS, the Bluetooth specification requires warning users upon issues with this key, because this can indicate ongoing MitM ( MitM ) attacks. This paper uncovers that none of the major Bluetooth stacks warns users, which violates the specification.

arxiv-2204-01090.title: Breaking the De-Pois Poisoning Defense
arxiv-2204-01090.creator: Alaa Anani, Mohamed Ghanem, Lotfy Abdel Khaliq
arxiv-2204-01090.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alaa Anani, Mohamed Ghanem, Lotfy Abdel Khaliq. Attacks on machine learning models have been, since their conception, a very persistent and evasive issue resembling an endless cat-and-mouse game. One major variant of such attacks is poisoning attacks which can indirectly manipulate an ML model. It has been observed over the years that the majority of proposed effective defense models are only effective when an attacker is not aware of them being employed.

arxiv-2210-06184.title: Images as Weight Matrices: Sequential Image Generation Through Synaptic Learning Rules
arxiv-2210-06184.creator: Kazuki Irie Jürgen Schmidhuber
arxiv-2210-06184.description: Abstract Work on fast weight programmers has demonstrated the effectiveness of key/value outer product-based learning rules for sequentially generating a weight matrix (WM) of a neural net (NN) by another NN or itself. However, the weight generation steps are typically not visually interpretable by humans, because the contents stored in the WM of an NN are not.

arxiv-2506-01994.title: Re-experiment Smart: a Novel Method to Enhance Data-driven Prediction of Mechanical Properties of Epoxy Polymers
arxiv-2506-01994.creator: Wanshan Cui, Yejin Jeong, Inwook Song, Gyuri Kim, Minsang Kwon, Donghun Lee
arxiv-2506-01994.description: Abstract Accurate prediction of polymer material properties through data-driven approaches greatly accelerates novel material development by reducing redundant experiments and trial-and-error processes. However, inevitable outliers in empirical measurements can severely skew machine learning results, leading to erroneous prediction models and suboptimal material designs.

arxiv-2506-23565.title: OcRFDet: Object-Centric Radiance Fields for Multi-View 3D Object Detection in Autonomous Driving
arxiv-2506-23565.creator: Mingqian Ji, Jian Yang, Shanshan Zhang
arxiv-2506-23565.description: Abstract Current multi-view 3D object detection methods typically transfer 2D features into 3D space using depth estimation or 3D position encoder, but in a fully data-driven and implicit manner, which limits the detection performance. Inspired by the success of radiance fields on 3D reconstruction, we assume they can be used to enhance the detector’s ability of 3D geometry estimation.

arxiv-2507-01894.title: Stellar-gas kinematic misalignments in eagle : enhanced SMBH growth in misaligned galaxies 2026 Stellar-gas kinematic misalignments in eagle : enhanced SMBH growth in misaligned galaxies – References
arxiv-2507-01894.creator: Maximilian K. Baker, Timothy A. Davis, Freeke van de Voort, Sandra I. Raimundo
arxiv-2507-01894.description: Abstract Stellar-gas kinematic misalignments are a transient phenomenon observed in ∼ 11 % \sim 11\% of the local galaxy population. According to current models, misaligned gas is expected to lose angular momentum and relax into the galactic plane on timescales of ∼ 0.1 \sim 0.1 Gyr, driving gas toward the central regions of the galaxy.

arxiv-2507-16744.title: University of Genova
arxiv-2507-16744.creator: Physics Department
arxiv-2507-16744.description: Abstract À ma grand-mère Gisèle Abstract In most cases Quantum Field Theories (QFTs) are considered without boundaries and have been successful in providing descriptions of fundamental interactions, including gravity and cosmology. This is because one is generally interested in bulk effects, where the boundary can be neglected.

arxiv-2601-01925.title: AR-MOT: Autoregressive Multi-object Tracking
arxiv-2601-01925.creator: Lianjie Jia, Yuhan Wu, Binghao Ran, Yifan Wang, Lijun Wang, Huchuan Lu
arxiv-2601-01925.description: Abstract As multi-object tracking (MOT) tasks continue to evolve toward more general and multi-modal scenarios, the rigid and task-specific architectures of existing MOT methods increasingly hinder their applicability across diverse tasks and limit flexibility in adapting to new tracking formulations.

pmc-11465569.title: A highly variable habitat selection in moose across diel and seasonal scales
pmc-11465569.creator: Tomasz Borowik, Rafał Kowalczyk, Mirosław Ratkiewicz, Weronika Maślanko, Norbert Duda, Michał Żmihorski
pmc-11465569.description: PurposeHabitat selection in animals is a hierarchal process that operates across multiple temporal and spatial scales, adapting to changes in environmental conditions, human disturbances, and predation risks. Despite its significance, previous research often oversimplifies temporal dynamics by categorizing them into broad seasonal and diel patterns, overlooking the continuous nature of temporal variability and habitat specificity.

pmc-11586819.title: Shape‐Morphing in Oxide Ceramic Kirigami Nanomembranes
pmc-11586819.creator: Minsoo Kim, Donghoon Kim, Mathieu Mirjolet, Nick A. Shepelin, Thomas Lippert, Hongsoo Choi, Josep Puigmartí‐Luis, Bradley J. Nelson, Xiang‐Zhong Chen, Salvador Pané
pmc-11586819.description: Interfacial strain engineering in ferroic nanomembranes can broaden the scope of ferroic nanomembrane assembly as well as facilitate the engineering of multiferroic‐based devices with enhanced functionalities. Geometrical engineering in these material systems enables the realization of 3‐D architectures with unconventional physical properties.

pmc-12505941.title: The clinical outcomes and tolerability of adding radiotherapy to first-line chemoimmunotherapy for treating patients with metastatic or relapsed esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: A retrospective cohort study
pmc-12505941.creator: Xin Hou, Zhen Ren, Rui Duan, Xin Ding
pmc-12505941.description: Objective:This investigation sought to assess the clinical outcomes and safety of adding radiotherapy (RT) to first-line chemoimmunotherapy (CIT) for advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC).Methodology:In this retrospective cohort study, patients with advanced ESCC (including metastatic or relapsed disease) who received first-line CIT at the Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University between 2020 and 2023 were enrolled.

pmc-12513959.title: The multifaceted impact of stress on immune function
pmc-12513959.creator: Marta Balcerowska, Paulina Kwaśnik
pmc-12513959.description: Stress is a response to physiological or psychological threats or challenging situations that enable one to cope with difficult circumstances. Various types of stressors promote a coordinated response in the body to maintain homeostasis. Experimental evidence suggests that the duration of stress is a pivotal factor influencing dysregulation in the immune system caused by stress.

pmc-12562753.title: Drug-Induced Epigenetic Alterations: A Set of Forensic Toxicological Fingerprints?—A Systematic Review
pmc-12562753.creator: Simone Grassi, Andrea Costantino, Alexandra Dimitrova, Emma Beatrice Croce, Francesca Iasi, Alessandra Puggioni, Francesco De Micco, Fabio Vaiano
pmc-12562753.description: Background/Objectives: Epigenetics refers to heritable modifications in gene expression that do not involve changes to the DNA sequence. Among these, DNA methylation, histone modifications, and non-coding RNAs play a key role in regulating gene activity and are influenced by environmental factors, including exposure to psychoactive substances.

pmc-12603421.title: Development of a machine learning-based nomogram for predicting chronic postsurgical pain after uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery
pmc-12603421.creator: Jie Jiang, Ye Shi, Yunhong Han, Hui Cao, Qin Wang, Feng Liu, Benhao Zhou
pmc-12603421.description: BackgroundChronic postsurgical pain (CPSP) remains a prevalent complication following uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (UVATS), significantly impairing patients’ quality of life. Currently, no reliable predictive tool exists. We aim to develop a machine learning-driven nomogram to stratify CPSP risk.MethodsPatients who underwent UVATS at Nanjing Brain Hospital Affiliated to Nanjing Medical University were analyzed in this retrospective cohort study.

pmc-12702216.title: Dataset for classification of forming tool types for aircraft parts based on neural network models using CAD
pmc-12702216.creator: Lee DongGyu, Lee HyunSup, Shin JaeHo, Shin MinSeok, Kang JiWon, Kim YoungSoon
pmc-12702216.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study presents a data collection using CAD image-based deep learning and machine learning models to classify forming tool types for aircraft parts. Focusing on sheet metal components i.e. which constitute a substantial portion of aircraft structures and are often produced via fluid-cell hydroforming, this dataset uses visual information embedded in CAD images, particularly flange geometries, to classify tool types without requiring physical prototypes or specialized sensors.

pmc-13065578.title: Randomised crossover trial of neurally adjusted ventilatory assist (NAVA) for neonates with congenital diaphragmatic hernias: the NAN-C study
pmc-13065578.creator: Sandeep Shetty, Allan Jenkinson, Grace Poole, Theodore Dassios, Chris Harris, Anay Kulkarni, Donovan Duffy, Anne Greenough
pmc-13065578.description: Retrospective studies comparing NAVA to assist control ventilation (ACV) in neonates with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) have shown that ventilatory mode may improve respiratory parameters. The aim of this study is to determine if infants with CDH studied post-operatively had a lower oxygenation index (OI) on NAVA compared to ACV.

pmc-13147959.title: Limitations of the refolding pipeline for de novo protein design
pmc-13147959.creator: Kerlen T. Korbeld, Vsevolod Viliuga, Maximilian J. L. J. Fürst
pmc-13147959.description: With the emergence of powerful deep learning‐based tools, computational protein design has become a widely accessible technique. Nowadays, it is possible to perform both sequence and structure design in a matter of minutes, making the technology attractive to the broader scientific community.

pmc-13242328.title: Cascade mentoring: a proposal for transforming radiology education in line with the European training curriculum
pmc-13242328.creator: Alberto Vieira, Ana Catarina Vieira
pmc-13242328.description: Although mentoring remains a fundamental part of medical training, the traditional approach of a senior mentor guiding a junior trainee often fails to meet the diverse and evolving needs of learners in radiology. While peer and near-peer mentoring approaches have shown promise, they often lack a scalable, structured framework.

pmc-13396388.title: BMA-YOLO: an object detection model for microscopic images of mouse embryos
pmc-13396388.creator: Yingsai Zhao, Weijun Zeng, Yuan Wang, Jiawei Wu, Weiguo Liang, Linyu Xu, Haixuan Sun
pmc-13396388.description: In vitro embryo culture is a pivotal technology in life sciences and medical research. However, automated monitoring remains challenging due to factors such as bubble interference and the frequent omission of small or peripheral embryos. To overcome these limitations, this study introduces BMA-YOLO, an enhanced model built upon the YOLOv8 architecture.

pmc-13409532.title: Interleukin-1β Gene (IL-1B) rs16944 (-511 C > T) Promoter Polymorphism Is Associated with Cutaneous Melanoma Susceptibility, Stage, and Anatomical Localization in a Northern Italian Case–Control Study
pmc-13409532.creator: Sabina Cauci, Cinzia Buligan, Patrizia Nacci, Gianluca Petris, Giuseppe Stinco
pmc-13409532.description: Simple SummaryWe determined the genotype and allele frequencies of the interleukin-1β gene (IL-1B) promoter polymorphism rs16944 (-511, C > T) in cutaneous melanoma patients and healthy controls from Northeastern Italy, a region with a high incidence of melanoma. The CC genotype and C allele were more frequent in melanoma cases than in healthy controls.

pmc-13441118.title: Feasibility, Usability, and Acceptability of an Adaptive Mobile Health Medication Adherence Intervention for Youth: Iterative Mixed Methods Human-Centered Design Study
pmc-13441118.creator: Caitlin S Sayegh, Shinyi Wu, Stephanie Lopez, Aridenne Dews, Jay Fleming, Daniela Cortez, Jan Portillo, Tamara Menendez, Marvin Belzer, Amy E West, Stephanie Law
pmc-13441118.description: BackgroundAdolescents and young adults with chronic health conditions often struggle to adhere to their daily oral medications. Transdiagnostic mobile health (mHealth) interventions have the potential to promote medication adherence by reaching youth at a large scale.ObjectiveThis study aimed at designing an adaptive medication adherence mHealth intervention (Adaptive Cell Phone Support), guided by iterative feasibility, usability, and acceptability feedback.

pmc-13470547.title: Field Epidemiological Investigation Training Demand Survey for Central and Local Epidemiological Investigation and Response Teams
pmc-13470547.creator: Yoo-Yeon Kim, Mi Yu, Jin Lee, Ho Kyoung Song, Eun Kyoung Kim, 유연 김, 미 유, 진 이, 호경 송, 은경 김
pmc-13470547.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesThe Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency conducts simulation training to enhance the response capabilities of Epidemiological Investigation and Response Teams (ERTs). We analyzed training demands among Central and Local ERTs following nine scenario-based training sessions in 2025.MethodsA survey was administered to 269 participants: 97 training debriefing attendees on-site (November 28, 2025) and 172 Central ERTs online (December 1–5, 2025) using a self-developed questionnaire that covered respondent characteristics, training topics, and methods.

pmc-13522091.title: Mediterranean diet adherence, healthy sleep, and lung cancer risk: a prospective study of 192,034 UK Biobank participants
pmc-13522091.creator: Yiming Chen, Enyu Tong, Xiaoman Jin, Yufeng Rao, Evan Y. W. Yu, Abdulmohsen H. Al-Zalabani, Maurice Zeegers, Anke Wesselius
pmc-13522091.description: PurposeDiet and sleep have each been associated with cancer risk, but their joint association with lung cancer risk remains unclear. We investigated the association between a joint Mediterranean diet-sleep pattern and lung cancer risk in the UK Biobank. We also evaluated whether siesta modified the association between Mediterranean diet adherence and lung cancer risk.MethodsParticipants were drawn from the UK Biobank.
